## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Bherivādakajātaka* (Ja 59), also designated as the *Bherivādajātaka*, is a story in the Pali Jātaka collection [Anandajoti 2010]. According to the traditional introductory narrative (*paccuppannavatthu*), the Buddha recounted the story while staying at Jetavana regarding a headstrong or self-willed monk, noting that this was not the first time the monk had acted obstinately.

In the story of the past (*atītavatthu*), a drummer earns money by playing at a festival, but his son's excessive drumming attracts thieves who beat and rob them, illustrating the lesson that excess leads to loss [Anandajoti 2010]. The moral is encapsulated in the verse opening *Dhame dhame nātidhame, atidhantam hi pāpakam* [Anandajoti 2010].
